text:
alex: Heads up — after landing the FlashAttention kernel selector and the paged-KV refactor we started seeing a small-sequence latency spike on a subset of traffic this morning. Profiling attached. :thinking:

devon: Can you paste the p50/p95/p99 numbers and which model variant is affected?

alex: quick numbers from the trace (single-GPU, 8k context, mixed seq lengths):
```
model: gpt-medium-8k
path: flashenabled + paged-kv
small-seq (1-8 tokens) p50 8ms p95 24ms p99 120ms
previous (no-flash / old-kv) p99 ~40ms

notable: long tail correlates with batches that contain both "flash-compatible" and "paged-kv-paged" requests.
```

maya: is the kernel swap happening inside a batch? that could stall the whole batch while we reload kernels or switch execution path.

alex: yep. flamegraph shows a 90ms stall between token steps where kernel selection transitions. link: https://internal/graphs/1812349999-flame.png :fire:

lorenzo: bench-bot, did the synthetic microbench for kernel-switch churn?

bench-bot: synthetic run results:
```
batch size 16 mixed kernels: avg latency +22% tail +3.1x
batch size 16 homogeneous flash: baseline
batcher grouping by kernel key reduces tail by ~70%
```

devon: So our continuous-batcher is currently forming batches by arrival time and token budget only, not by kernel capability. For models with multiple kernels (flash / fallback) we should bias formation to group compatible requests or preemptively flush if mixing would cause a kernel swap.

alex: Proposed quick fixes: 1) add a kernel_compatibility tag on requests at enqueue time (cheap check: model config + seq len) 2) prefer same-key grouping up to token_budget, 3) if mixed-keys detected and SLO-sensitive request present => preemptive flush smaller batch.

maya: Also consider adding a per-queue "kernel-swap penalty" estimate to the cost model. Batcher currently optimizes token_budget -> latency but treats kernel swap as zero cost. If we add a penalty (ms) we can make the dynamic programming pick homogeneous groups more often.

devon: agree. We should calibrate the penalty using bench-bot numbers and live traces. Start with 80ms penalty and tune down. Also add a metric: batch.kernel_swap_count and batch.swap_stall_ms.

lorenzo: Edge-case: paged-KV sometimes pins different memory layout that forces a compatibility check after batch formation (because we lazily allocate). We should move that check to enqueue time too, otherwise the swap still occurs post-formation.

alex: Good catch. I'll open a small PR to move layout compatibility check into Batcher.enqueue and to tag requests.

maya: One more thought: for small sequences, batching by kernel might reduce effective batching opportunities. Could degrade throughput if we split too aggressively. So add a tunable: min_homogeneous_batch_utilization (like require at least X% of budget to be used before splitting).

devon: plan:
- alex: enqueue-tag PR + metric emits (today)
- bench-bot: run calibration matrix (batch size, token budget, penalty ms) across 1-32 batch sizes and produce heatmaps (today)
- lorenzo: move paged-KV layout check out of executor and into enqueue (tomorrow)
- maya: add DP config option in batcher to include kernel-swap penalty (this week)

alex: I'll also add a canary route that forces homogeneous batcher behavior for 5% of production traffic to validate no throughput regressions.

bench-bot: calibration job queued: job/181234-batch-calib-01. Will post summary when done. :hammer_and_wrench:

devon: Thanks. If we can get a 50-80ms reduction on p99 for small-seq without losing throughput we're good. Keep thread updated and drop traces here.

alex: will do. dropping initial PR link: https://git.internal/r/3241 (WIP).
